full_judgment:
20. We are of the opinion that it is for the defence to make out which provisions of relevant law have not been complied with in conducting the search. Failure to do so would lead to a presumption that the provisions of section 165 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and section 25 of the Penal Code have been complied with. We do not see how, from the bare circumstances and on the basis of vague allegations of non-compliance, the search, if any, can be declared illegal. The only thing one can do is to be careful in dealing with the evidence of the search, so as to exclude the chance of its being as a result of malice. 

 23. In such a case presumption of regularity of official acts will be invoked otherwise the purpose of the section will be defeated. If a police officer conducts a search within the limit of another police station, if may be presumed, unless otherwise proved, that reasons have been recorded by that officer that delay would have occasioned and evidence destroyed, if he had waited to have the place searched by police having jurisdiction of the place.
